title: Describe controller-based and software defined architectures

questions.question: Which type of architecture is used with controller-based networks?

correct.explanation: Controller-based SDN campus/data-center fabrics commonly use spine-leaf (Clos) topology for equal-cost multipath east-west traffic.

incorrect.explanation: Three-tier (access-distribution-core) is classic hierarchical — modern controller fabrics favor spine-leaf for scale and ECMP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Applying legacy three-tier to SDN fabric
incorrect.whatItDoes: Three tier points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", Spine/Leaf satisfies what this question tests — Three tier does not.

incorrect.explanation: Collapsed core merges distribution/core — spine-leaf is the distinct SDN fabric pattern tested here.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Collapsed core points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", Spine/Leaf satisfies what this question tests — Collapsed core does not.

incorrect.explanation: SAN fabric is storage networking (FC/FCoE) — not the IP Ethernet architecture for controller-based LANs.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Dragging storage fabric into SDN campus question
incorrect.whatItDoes: SAN fabric points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", Spine/Leaf satisfies what this question tests — SAN fabric does not.

answerReview.examTip: Controller/SDN fabric → spine-leaf. Legacy campus → three-tier.

questions.question: Which is a correct statement about Spine/Leaf architecture?
choices: The Leaf switches connect to other Leaf switches.
There is only one Spine switch per network.
Spine switches provide access to hosts.
The Leaf switches never connect to other Leaf switches, only Spine switches.

correct.explanation: In spine-leaf, leaf switches connect hosts and uplink only to spines — leaf-to-leaf traffic hairpins through spines, never direct leaf links.

incorrect.explanation: Leaf switches do not interconnect to other leafs — that breaks the spine-leaf model and defeats ECMP fabric design.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The Leaf switches connect to other Leaf switches. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", The Leaf switches never connect to other Leaf switches, only Spine switches. satisfies what this question tests — The Leaf switches connect to other Leaf switches. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Production fabrics use multiple spines for redundancy and bisection bandwidth — not a single spine only.
incorrect.whatItDoes: There is only one Spine switch per network. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", The Leaf switches never connect to other Leaf switches, only Spine switches. satisfies what this question tests — There is only one Spine switch per network. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Spines aggregate leafs — hosts attach at the leaf tier, not the spine.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Hosts connecting directly to spine switches
incorrect.whatItDoes: Spine switches provide access to hosts. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", The Leaf switches never connect to other Leaf switches, only Spine switches. satisfies what this question tests — Spine switches provide access to hosts. does not.

answerReview.examTip: Spine-leaf: hosts on leaf, leafs connect only to spines, never leaf-to-leaf.

questions.question: Identify the flow of traffic in a Spine/Leaf network?

correct.explanation: In spine-leaf, every leaf connects to spines — east-west traffic flows leaf → spine → leaf, never leaf-to-leaf direct.

incorrect.explanation: Leaf switches do not transit through another leaf — traffic goes up to spine first.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Leaf to Leaf to Spine points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", Leaf to Spine to Leaf satisfies what this question tests — Leaf to Leaf to Spine does not.

incorrect.explanation: Spine switches interconnect leaves — they are not the endpoint path spine → leaf → spine for host traffic.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Spine to Leaf to Spine points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", Leaf to Spine to Leaf satisfies what this question tests — Spine to Leaf to Spine does not.

incorrect.explanation: Direct leaf-to-leaf links violate spine-leaf design — all paths traverse the spine.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Leaf to Leaf points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", Leaf to Spine to Leaf satisfies what this question tests — Leaf to Leaf does not.

answerReview.examTip: Spine-leaf east-west path → leaf–spine–leaf (full mesh between tiers).

questions.question: Which statement is correct about the SDN controller?
choices: The SDN controller configures the management plane of network devices.
The SDN controller monitors data plane traffic.
The SDN controller replaces the control plane of the SDN.
The SDN controller complements the control plane of the SDN device.

correct.explanation: The SDN controller replaces the distributed control plane — devices forward (data plane) per controller policy.

incorrect.explanation: Management plane (CLI, SNMP) may remain — the controller centralizes the control plane, not mgmt only.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The SDN controller configures the management plane of network devices. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", The SDN controller replaces the control plane of the SDN. satisfies what this question tests — The SDN controller configures the management plane of network devices. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Monitoring data-plane traffic is analytics — the controller owns control-plane decisions.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The SDN controller monitors data plane traffic. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", The SDN controller replaces the control plane of the SDN. satisfies what this question tests — The SDN controller monitors data plane traffic. does not.

incorrect.explanation: The controller centralizes/replaces control functions — it does not merely complement local routing.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Controller complements instead of replaces control plane
incorrect.whatItDoes: The SDN controller complements the control plane of the SDN device. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for sdn architecture.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "sdn architecture", The SDN controller replaces the control plane of the SDN. satisfies what this question tests — The SDN controller complements the control plane of the SDN device. does not.

answerReview.examTip: SDN split: data plane on switch | control plane on controller | mgmt often still local.
